stem: When removing a contaminated isolation gown, which technique best follows CDC guidance to reduce self-contamination?

options.A: Unfasten the gown, remove it with a peeling motion so the contaminated surface turns inward, hold it away from the body, roll it into a bundle, discard it, and perform hand hygiene.
options.B: Grasp the contaminated front and sleeves with bare hands, pull the gown toward the body, fold the outside surface outward, and then discard it.
options.C: Keep the gown on while leaving the patient-care area and remove it only after using shared equipment at the nursing station.
options.D: Remove the gown, place it with the contaminated surface exposed for reuse during the next entry, and perform hand hygiene only at the end of the shift.

rationale: CDC's PPE-removal guidance states that the gown front and sleeves are contaminated. The gown should be unfastened, removed with a peeling motion so it turns inside out, held away from the body, rolled into a bundle, discarded appropriately, and followed by hand hygiene. Therefore A is correct. B deliberately contacts the contaminated outer surface and brings it toward the body. C carries contaminated PPE outside the patient-care area. D conflicts with CDC guidance to discard used gowns and perform hand hygiene after PPE removal.
educational_objective: Remove a contaminated isolation gown by turning the contaminated surface inward, keeping it away from skin and clothing, discarding it appropriately, and performing hand hygiene after PPE removal.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

source_claim_supported: CDC instructs removal of a contaminated gown with a peeling motion that turns the contaminated surface inward, keeping the gown away from the body, rolling it into a bundle for disposal, and performing hand hygiene after PPE removal.

correction_summary: Replaced the generic Isolation Precautions locator with the exact CDC PPE-removal figure and rewrote the stem/options around the explicit gown-removal sequence. Removed the unsupported wording that exact sequence may vary and replaced the absurd gown-shaking distractor with procedural alternatives that test contamination boundaries. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
